feedback.body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

If the sampling kernel fails or is invalid, `local` can contain `-1` as a sentinel value. Directly using `local.view(-1, 1).long()` in `gather` will cause `-1` to index the last element of `gathered_indices` (i.e., `top_k - 1`), silently mapping an invalid sample to a valid vocabulary index. We should preserve `-1` (or any negative sentinel values) in the mapped output.

```suggestion
    def _map(local):
        mapped = (
            gathered_indices.gather(1, local.clamp(min=0).view(-1, 1).long())
            .squeeze(1)
            .to(torch.int32)
        )
        return torch.where(local >= 0, mapped, -1)
```

feedback.author: gemini-code-assist[bot]
feedback.body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

When parallel sampling is enabled (i.e., `parallel_sample_num > 1`), the batch size is expanded to `batch_size * parallel_sample_num`. However, `self.session_params` is not expanded during normalization. As a result, accessing `self.session_params[i]` for indices `i >= len(self.session_params)` will raise an `IndexError`.

Using modulo indexing with `i % len(self.session_params)` safely maps the expanded request items back to their corresponding original session parameters and avoids the `IndexError`.

```suggestion
            session_params=(
                self.session_params[i % len(self.session_params)]
                if isinstance(self.session_params, list) and self.session_params
                else self.session_params
            ),
```

feedback.author: chengcuiping
feedback.body:
I don't think the premise of this suggestion holds. `GenerateReqInput.__getitem__`
is never called with `i >= batch_size`, including when `parallel_sample_num > 1`.

In `tokenizer_manager._handle_batch_request`, the n>1 branch does:

    objs = [obj[i] for i in range(batch_size)]

and then expands via `copy.copy(objs[i])` with regenerated rids — the expansion
never goes through `__getitem__`. The batch-tokenization path
(`_batch_tokenize_and_process`) likewise only indexes `range(batch_size)`.
The `* parallel_sample_num` tiling in `_normalize_batch_inputs` is probably what
suggests expanded indexing, but the consumption side only ever reads the first
`batch_size` entries.

So with a correct-length list, `i % len(...)` is a no-op. With a *wrong-length*
list, it silently wraps around and assigns a request to another request's
session — silent cross-session contamination (sessions control KV-cache reuse
and context continuation) instead of a loud error. And with an empty list, the
current version raises ZeroDivisionError.

I'd suggest reverting to the original plain `self.session_params[i]`, and
handling malformed input by validation instead: `_validate_session_params`
already exists on `GenerateReqInput` but is never called from
`normalize_batch_and_arguments`. Wiring it up with a
`len(session_params) == batch_size` check (plus all-elements-are-dicts; the
current check only inspects `[0]` and IndexErrors on `[]`) turns every
malformed case into a clear ValueError at request time. I have these validator
changes and edge-case tests passing locally against main — happy to share.

feedback.author: he-yufeng
feedback.body:
Addressed the parallel sampling case in 76f8e6c74.

`normalize_batch_and_arguments()` expands batched fields as `values * parallel_sample_num`, so the expanded order is `p1, p2, p1, p2` for `n=2`. `__getitem__` now maps list `session_params` with modulo indexing instead of direct `session_params[i]`, avoiding an `IndexError` while preserving the original request/session pairing. I also added a regression test for the expanded batch case.

Verified locally on Windows:

- `python -m ruff check python\sglang\srt\managers\io_struct.py test\registered\unit\managers\test_io_struct.py`
- `python -m py_compile python\sglang\srt\managers\io_struct.py test\registered\unit\managers\test_io_struct.py`
- `git diff --check`

I also attempted the focused pytest with `PYTHONPATH=python`; collection is blocked on Windows because importing `sglang.srt.utils.common` requires the Unix-only `resource` module. The new test should run in the project's Linux CI environment.

feedback.author: he-yufeng
feedback.body:
Thanks for the detailed review. I agree with your read of the call path: the expanded `parallel_sample_num` items are copied after the original `range(batch_size)` indexing, so this PR's premise does not hold for a valid request.

More importantly, the modulo fallback can make malformed `session_params` worse by silently assigning one request's session metadata to another request. A clear validation error is the safer behavior here.

I'm closing this PR to avoid keeping a misleading fix alive. If I revisit this area, I'll do it as a validation-focused patch against `_validate_session_params` rather than wrapping indices in `__getitem__`.

feedback.body:
Hi @milesial — heads up: this PR introduced a regression on `main` that breaks the `H100_PCIe-PyTorch-Ray-1` stage, so I opened a revert: #15306.

**Root cause:** this PR adds `reset_prefix_cache()` to `BaseWorker`. Since `RayGPUWorker(RpcWorkerMixin, BaseWorker)` inherits it, the method now exists on the worker class. The Ray worker-extension injection check (`RayGPUWorker._inject_worker_extension`, `ray_gpu_worker.py:196-203`) hard-fails on any extension whose attribute name already exists on the worker class, and the RL/verl `WorkerExtension` also defines `reset_prefix_cache`:

```
ValueError: Worker class RayGPUWorker already defines 'reset_prefix_cache',
which conflicts with extension WorkerExtension.
  -> RuntimeError: RayGPUWorker died during initialization
```

This kills the Ray worker at init, so all `test_llm_update_weights*`, `test_llm_partial_update_weights*`, and `async_llm` tests in that stage fail before reaching their logic (e.g. post-merge `L0_Test-x86_64-Single-GPU #3385`).

Note the `H100_PCIe-PyTorch-Ray-1` stage was already failing in this PR's final CI run (`L0_MergeRequest_PR #42818`, commit `dd8936e`) — that failure wasn't flaky, it was this collision — but the PR was merged with `/bot skip --comment "Known flaky tests"`, so it reached `main`.

**Re-landing suggestion:** either pick a non-colliding method name on `BaseWorker`, or make the extension-injection check tolerate an intentional override instead of raising on every name match. Happy to help review the follow-up.
